findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED (grep of the whole tree excluding node_modules): the committed prior review text contains the owner's lab-wide custom User-Agent string `<lab user-agent>` (line 80, inside a `curl -A '...'` example) and, at line 96, the grep alternation `ts\.net|/home/|@gmail|<lab-specific terms>`, which names three internal lab hosts/tools. Publishing the UA string lets any site operator correlate that fingerprint in their logs with this author and handle.

findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs:289-301 (writeReceiptAtomic renames over the receipt without checking the target's mode) vs README.md:68 and CHANGELOG.md ('On a read-only receipt the requirement is enforced in memory with a warning'), SKILL.md:71
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: with the run directory writable and only `receipt.json` set to mode 444, `check receipt.json --require tablet:Overview` replaced the file without any warning (sha256 changed, mode became 664) and exited 3; `attest` on the same 444 file likewise succeeded and rewrote it. Only a read-only *directory* triggers the documented warning path (verified: chmod 555 dir gives 'cannot write receipt ... EACCES' exit 64 for attest and the warning plus normal gate code for check). A user who chmods a receipt to freeze evidence gets it silently replaced and its permissions reset; the docs say 'read-only receipt' when the behaviour is 'read-only directory'.
findings.amendment: In writeReceiptAtomic, before renaming, `if (existsSync(receiptPath)) accessSync(receiptPath, constants.W_OK)` so a 444 receipt raises EACCES and flows into the existing warning/usage-error path; or change README.md:68, SKILL.md:71 and CHANGELOG to say 'read-only run directory'.
findings.mechanical_test: `cp -r run ro; chmod 444 ro/receipt.json; node scripts/capture.mjs check ro/receipt.json --require tablet:Overview; stat -c %a ro/receipt.json` prints 444 and stderr contains 'read-only'; `node scripts/capture.mjs attest ro/receipt.json --path <png> --verdict pass --note 'ten chars plus' --by t` exits 64 with 'cannot write receipt'.

findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs:531-534 (console/pageerror text goes through redact() only) vs README.md:282 ('the receipt records only whether one was used, never the string') and --help line 46 ('not recorded in the receipt')
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: a page whose script runs `console.error('navigator ua is ' + navigator.userAgent)` captured with `--user-agent 'LabProbe/9.9 (secret-lab@example.invalid)'` produced `diagnostics[0].events[0].text = 'navigator ua is LabProbe/9.9 (secret-lab@example.invalid)'` in receipt.json. The tool itself does not record the override (verified `user_agent_override: true`, string absent from `config`), but any page that echoes its UA to the console (analytics and debug builds commonly do) reinserts it. For an owner whose environment mandates a distinctive UA this is the leak path that matters, and the README sentence reads as a guarantee.
findings.amendment: In redact(), when a User-Agent override is configured, replace every occurrence of the configured string with `[USER-AGENT]` before other rules; and soften README.md:282 to 'the collector never writes the string itself; page output that echoes it is redacted best-effort'.
findings.mechanical_test: Fixture with `console.error(navigator.userAgent)`; capture with `--user-agent 'Probe/1.0 (someone@example.invalid)'`; `! grep -q 'someone@example.invalid' receipt.json`.

findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs:468-475 (out-dir reuse: priorReceipt is assigned before required_coverage canonicalisation, and the catch swallows the UsageError) vs scripts/capture.mjs:351-352 (check rejects the same receipt with exit 64)
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: a prior receipt whose `required_coverage` is `['desktop:overview','junk-no-colon']` makes `check` exit 64 (fail closed), but re-capturing into that out-dir succeeds and writes a new receipt with `required_coverage` absent, i.e. the stored requirement is silently dropped; the same happens for a non-string entry (`['desktop:overview', 5]`). It takes a hand-edited receipt to reach this state, so it is inside the documented 'anyone who can write the receipt can rewrite it' boundary, but the two commands disagree about whether such a receipt is trustworthy, and the reuse path is the one that quietly widens the gate.
findings.amendment: Move the canonicalisation out of the swallowing try: if `priorReceipt.required_coverage` exists but is not an array of canonicalisable strings, throw `UsageError('refusing to reuse --out-dir: prior receipt has an unreadable required_coverage')`.
findings.mechanical_test: Set `required_coverage` to `['desktop:overview','junk']` in a run's receipt.json; re-capture into that --out-dir; expect exit 64 and the original receipt untouched. Add to tests/test_capture.sh section 21.
